# `test` standard library

The `test` module provides a lightweight assertion and test-reporting harness with
pass/fail counters, descriptive failure diagnostics, and exit-code summaries.

```{.dva .run}
#use test

test::eq(2 + 2, 4, "basic addition")
test::ne("edva", "rust", "distinct strings")
test::approx(3.14159, 3.1416, 0.001)
test::summary!
```

## Function catalog

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `test::check(cond[, msg])` | `<>, [String] => <>` | Asserts that boolean condition `cond` is `<+>` |
| `test::ok(res[, msg])` | `R, [String] => <>` | Asserts that ramification `res` is in its positive state (`<+>`, `<+ v +>`, `<+ v ->`) |
| `test::err(res[, msg])` | `R, [String] => <>` | Asserts that ramification `res` is in its negative state (`<->`, `<-->`, `<- e +>`) |
| `test::eq(actual, expected[, msg])` | `#! T: Type, T, T[, String] => <>` | Asserts structural equality `actual == expected` across scalars, records, tuples, enums, options, arrays, slices, and maps |
| `test::ne(actual, expected[, msg])` / `test::neq` | `#! T: Type, T, T[, String] => <>` | Asserts structural inequality `actual != expected` |
| `test::struct_eq(a, b)` | `#! T: Type, T, T => <>` | Compile-time specialized deep structural equality check |
| `test::format_val(v)` | `#! T: Type, T => String` | Compile-time specialized structural value formatter used in failure diagnostics |
| `test::approx(actual, expected, eps, msg)` | `Float, Float, Float, String => <>` | Asserts `|actual - expected| <= eps` |
| `test::fail(msg)` | `String => <>` | Unconditionally records a test failure with `msg` |
| `test::suite(name, body)` | `String, (() => ()) => ()` | Runs `body` under named suite header `=== Suite: <name> ===` |
| `test::reset!` | `() => ()` | Resets passed and failed counters to `0` |
| `test::passed!` / `test::failed!` / `test::total!` | `() => Int` | Queries current assertion counters |
| `test::summary!` | `() => ()` | Prints `PASS: N passed, 0 failed` (or `FAIL: ...` and exits `1`) |
| `test::finish!` | `() => Int` | Prints summary and returns `0` if all passed or `1` if any failed |
